matches.quote: Anisotropic QPI in the Sn-doped samples is not shown to reflect an anisotropic electronic state rather than an anisotropic arrangement of scatterers or local strain.
Ideally it would be supported by spectroscopic maps (QPI or energy-resolved Bragg amplitudes), so that the two dopant families are compared using the same electronic observable.
No quantitative, unbiased measure of nematic order, and no comparison with the anisotropy that isotropic disorder alone would produce.
At x ≈ 0.1, which connects the two regimes, the paper's own marker of nematicity, the ½Q_Bragg feature, is absent (p. 4; Extended Data Fig. 1).
The Sn-sample evidence is a finite-q unidirectional modulation, and residual short-range CDW is not excluded; yet the paper calls it "q = 0 nematicity".
Unidirectional ½Q correlations are exactly what short-range, locally 1Q 2×2 CDW fluctuations or disorder- or strain-pinned remnants of the CDW would look like.
Unequal Bragg amplitudes in a topograph can come from several sources, none of them electronic nematicity: local lattice distortion or strain around Ti or Ti clusters
The constant-energy contours and autocorrelations are computed for x ≈ 0.25 (p. 5), while the data are at x = 0.33 and 0.68.
"Parent state of kagome superconductors" (title, abstract, p. 7) means a state that forms at higher temperature and from which the CDW, superconductivity and other low-temperature orders emerge.
The p. 5 statement that the ½Q_Bragg vector connects "exactly" the M pockets depends on where the chemical potential sits, and Sn hole doping changes that.

notes: C6 asks for inverse Fourier transforms of each 1/2 Q_Bragg component over Figs. 3a,c; P22 asks for Lawler-Fujita/lock-in demodulation amplitude maps at the three 1/2 Q_Bragg vectors over the entire FOVs of Figs. 3a,c, which is mathematically equivalent. C7 calls the finite-q 1/2 Q_Bragg unidirectional domains 'smectic' rather than nematic; P3 raises the exact same physical objection that the Sn data show finite-q unidirectional modulations rather than q=0 nematicity.
